spot.source: Closing price 06-Aug-2026 from the supplied EGX daily series (open 81.80, high 82.50, low 78.30). Three reviewers quoted 81.10 with a 78.51-84.00 range; that is the 05-Aug row of the same file

shares_mn.source: 260,812,477 shares, corroborated FIVE ways: issued capital EGP 2,608,124,770 at EGP 10 par; the Jul-2025 tender offer of 58,416,664 shares at 22.4%; quoted market capitalisation over price; and the reconstruction 133.07mn pre-issue + 127.74mn subscribed. Revision 1 wrongly described the pre-issue count as 92.61mn by subtracting shares OFFERED (168.20mn) instead of shares SUBSCRIBED (127.74mn, a 75.95% take-up)

shares_fy23.source: Weighted-average shares FY2023, pre-rights-issue. Corroborated by the 2022 tender offer (56.063mn = 42.12%) and by disclosed EPS

shares_fy24.source: Weighted-average shares FY2024. Disclosed EPS of EGP 23.13 on attributable profit implies 132.7mn

shares_fy25.source: Weighted-average shares FY2025, the rights issue having completed during the year

tax_eff.source: EFFECTIVE tax rate on the FY2025 closure. Disclosed pre-tax profit of 3,378.7 against profit after tax of 2,298.2 gives 32.0%. Revision 1 used the statutory 22.5% here, which understated every derived operating line

rev_fy23.source: EGX filing reported by Global Cement, cemnet/International Cement Review, Daily News Egypt and Arab Finance — FY2023 net sales

rev_fy24.source: EGX filing reported by Global Cement, cemnet/International Cement Review, Daily News Egypt and Arab Finance — FY2024 net sales

rev_fy25.source: EGX filing reported by Global Cement, cemnet/International Cement Review, Daily News Egypt and Arab Finance — FY2025 revenue, +41.4%

pat_fy23.source: EGX filing reported by Global Cement, cemnet/International Cement Review, Daily News Egypt and Arab Finance — FY2023 net loss after tax

pat_fy24.source: EGX filing reported by Global Cement, cemnet/International Cement Review, Daily News Egypt and Arab Finance — FY2024 net profit after tax

pat_fy25.source: EGX filing reported by Global Cement, cemnet/International Cement Review, Daily News Egypt and Arab Finance — FY2025 net profit after tax

ebitda_fy24.source: FY2024 EBITDA, the one disclosed margin anchor

ta_fy24.source: EGX filing reported by Global Cement, cemnet/International Cement Review, Daily News Egypt and Arab Finance — FY2024 total assets

tl_fy24.source: EGX filing reported by Global Cement, cemnet/International Cement Review, Daily News Egypt and Arab Finance — FY2024 total liabilities; the triple closes to equity of 4,775.06 exactly

cash_fy25.source: FY2025 balance-sheet data from S&P Global Market Intelligence as carried by two independent aggregations (stockanalysis.com, simplywall.st), which agree — FY2025 cash and equivalents EGP 3.85bn. Revision 1 derived 5,344 by dividing solved treasury income by an assumed yield and then applying an undisclosed 1.35x roll. The reported figure is obtainable at the same evidentiary standard as revenue and profit

debt_fy25.source: Total debt. The company is NET CASH

eq_fy25_rep.source: FY2025 balance-sheet data from S&P Global Market Intelligence as carried by two independent aggregations (stockanalysis.com, simplywall.st), which agree — FY2025 shareholders' equity ~EGP 5.24bn

nci.source: Non-controlling interests deducted in the bridge. Revision 1 omitted them. One reviewer proposed 2,008 (15% of enterprise value) but derived it from nothing; the disclosed evidence — FY2023 group loss 121.42 against an attributable loss of ~117, and FY2024 attributable EPS 23.13 against group profit 3,070 — puts the minority share of profit BELOW 1%. Set at 120 and sensitised

swcc_eur.source: EUR 30mn for the 25.40% Sinai White stake, completed 13-Aug-2024

swcc_book.source: Carrying value of the 25.4% stake. Revision 1 asserted the profit bridge was 'insensitive to it within a +/-EGP 200mn range'. That was FALSE and untested: in revision 1 the chain ran book value -> gain -> SOLVED treasury income -> cash -> every lens, and a +/-200mn move was worth -4.9% to +9.8%. Revision 2 takes cash from the reported balance sheet instead, so this input now touches only the FY2024 gain/treasury split and nothing downstream

cap_cement_mt.source: Cement grinding capacity, El Hassana, two lines

cap_clinker_mt.source: Kiln clinker capacity. The PAIR with cement capacity OBSERVES the clinker factor rather than assuming it, and settles which base a USD-per-tonne benchmark is quoted on

thermal_gj_t_clinker.source: Specific thermal energy, 3.2-3.6 GJ/t clinker for a dry preheater/precalciner kiln

fuel_usd_gj.source: Delivered solid fuel, petcoke/coal ~USD 128/t at ~32 GJ/t

power_tariff.source: Egyptian industrial electricity tariff after subsidy reform

rawmat_egp_t.source: Quarrying, raw meal and additives per tonne of cement

packaging_egp_t.source: Bag cost per tonne of bagged cement

distribution_egp_t.source: Outbound freight and selling per tonne, set above a typical Egyptian plant because El Hassana is distant from the Cairo and Delta demand centres

fixed_usd_t_capacity.source: Fixed cash cost per tonne of INSTALLED capacity so it does not vanish when volume falls. Industry band USD 10-20/t. 14.60 is the level the FY2025 reconciliation implies against an independently built variable stack — reported, not solved away

price_dom_egp_t.source: Domestic realised price ex-works. FY2025 is the level the disclosed revenue implies given the volume build — 13.9% below the ~EGP 4,070/t market average, which is what an ex-works price net of freight and rebates looks like. The path then grows 4.5-6.0% nominal, a REAL decline against CBE inflation

price_exp_usd_t.source: Export FOB per tonne, declining because the EU carbon border mechanism raises the landed cost of Egyptian cement into Europe from 2026

fx_path.source: USD/EGP path. Raises the EGP cost of imported fuel AND the EGP value of export revenue; the legs partly offset

cost_infl.source: Cumulative local cost inflation index on the EGP cost lines

dna_pct.source: D&A as a share of revenue

capex_pct.source: Capex as a share of revenue. No capital-expenditure disclosure is obtainable

wc_pct_drev.source: Change in working capital over change in revenue

cash_yield_fy25.source: Yield earned on cash through FY2025

sov_spread_cds.source: Egypt CDS-implied sovereign default spread, Damodaran January-2026, CDS column. NETTED OUT of the local risk-free rate so sovereign default risk is not charged twice. One reviewer called this a manipulation; two others cleared it explicitly, and it is Damodaran's own construction — the country premium in the ERP is DERIVED from this same spread

erp_cds.source: Damodaran Egypt, CDS-BASED, January-2026: mature-market 4.23% + 3.40% x (9.71/6.37) = 9.4127%. Revision 1 cited 'Damodaran, Egypt row' without naming the variant; a checker following that citation lands on the rating-based 13.94%

beta.source: Adopted beta. The own-stock regression FAILS the usability gate (R-squared 0.038 against a 0.05 floor) though n=256 and SE 0.153 both pass. The lead-lag corrected estimate is 0.837 and its 90% interval contains 1.00. Rounding up to 1.00 COSTS 1.84% of the central; that price is now stated rather than left implicit

kd.source: Marginal pre-tax cost of debt. Debt is 0.18% of capital, so a +/-700bp error moves the WACC by under 2bp

kd_path.source: Cost-of-debt path; the WACC glide inherits its SHAPE from this

kd_term.source: Terminal cost of debt, the Egyptian long-run corporate norm

rf_term.source: Terminal risk-free rate, norm-built from the CBE's OPERATIVE Q4-2026 inflation target of 7% plus a ~5.5pp emerging-market real-rate convention. Revision 1 used the later 5% target while its own text cited 'the 7% and then 5% targets'. REVIEWABLE CHOICE: reverting to 10.5% adds ~1.8%

erp_term.source: Terminal equity risk premium, normalised below the crisis level

g_term.source: Terminal growth, 5% nominal against a terminal risk-free rate embedding disinflation — approximately zero real. Held at 5% rather than raised with the inflation target: 7% would put terminal growth above the disinflation path the same model assumes

stub_years.source: Elapsed fraction of FY2026 at the valuation date (7 months). Revision 1 discounted FY2026 a full year from a 6-Aug-2026 valuation date and added a 31-Dec-2025 cash balance

repl_usd_t.source: Replacement cost per annual tonne of CEMENT capacity, USD 120-150 band

ev_t_just.source: Justified enterprise value per annual tonne of cement capacity

ev_ebitda_just.source: Justified EV/EBITDA. Revision 1 used 5.0x anchored on a peer quoted at 5.03x. That anchor does not reproduce: the peer's own market capitalisation over profit gives 3.48x, not the 6.44x printed beside it, and the implied EBITDA margin would be 68% for a cement company. 4.2x is struck between the reproducible peer earnings multiple and the asserted EBITDA multiple, and is disclosed as weakly anchored

pe_just.source: Justified price/earnings on normalised OPERATING earnings

norm_mgn.source: Mid-cycle EBITDA margin: the midpoint of the FY2024 outturn (24.8%) and the corrected FY2025 peak (30.9%). Revision 1 struck 26.5% off an FY2025 margin understated by the statutory-rate error

norm_rev_haircut.source: Haircut to the FY2025 revenue base for the normalised lens. Revision 1 applied a mid-cycle MARGIN to a PEAK revenue base — half a normalisation, in the lens whose stated purpose is refusing to capitalise a peak

cash_growth_fy25.source: RETIRED in revision 2 — cash is now the reported balance, not a rolled derivation. Kept at 1.0 so nothing scales it

treas_fy23.source: FY2023 treasury income on its own smaller cash balance

peer_mbsc_rev.source: Misr Beni Suef FY2025 net sales

peer_mbsc_pat.source: Misr Beni Suef FY2025 attributable profit

peer_mbsc_pe.source: Misr Beni Suef trailing price/earnings RECOMPUTED as market capitalisation over attributable profit. The 6.44x printed by data providers cannot be reconciled with the market capitalisation printed beside it — 6.44 x 3,946 = 25,412 against a stated 13,730

peer_mbsc_evebitda.source: Misr Beni Suef EV/EBITDA as quoted. Carried with a caution: no enterprise value, EBITDA or net-cash figure is published for it, and pairing it with the stated profit implies a 68% EBITDA margin, which no cement company earns

mto_price.source: Vicat mandatory tender offer, July 2025. A disclosed reference point and an overhang, never a fair value

w_asset.source: Weight, asset lens. Revision 1 gave it 15% while arguing in the same document that restarted lines cost 'a fraction' of new build and that the asset lens 'should not be read as a floor'. Cut to 8%. REVIEWABLE CHOICE: 15% adds ~3.6%, zero subtracts ~2.6%

experts.label: Expert 1
experts.summary: Values the plant, not the earnings stream. A 3.8Mt grey-cement plant costs about USD 130 per annual tonne to build; nobody pays replacement cost for capacity in a market carrying 76Mt against 54Mt of consumption. The market pays USD 83/t.
experts.falsifier: Find an Egyptian line built, bought or restarted below USD 95 per annual tonne. The 12.6Mt revival programme is the live test: restarting a mothballed line costs a fraction of building one, which is why this lens is a ceiling and not a floor — and why it now carries 8% of the weight rather than 15%.

experts.label: Expert 2
experts.summary: Refuses to capitalise a peak, and now refuses it on BOTH legs: the margin is normalised to 27.8% and the revenue base is cut 8% because FY2025 embeds the post-quota price spike.
experts.falsifier: Two consecutive years of realised prices above EGP 3,900/t WITH the revival proceeding would prove the mid-cycle base too low.

experts.label: Expert 3
experts.summary: Starts from the balance sheet. Net cash of EGP 4.9bn is 24% of the market capitalisation and 43% of fair equity value. Terminal return on capital of 9.3% sits below the 19.0% cost of capital, so growth destroys value and the right policy is to harvest and distribute.
experts.falsifier: The lens rests on the cash being distributable. Vicat holds 77.6% and a minority cannot force a dividend. If none is declared on FY2026 profits, or the cash funds expansion into a glut, it is worth less than face.
